title: Cellular Reproduction
seo_title: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Cellular Reproduction Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Living and Non-Living Things
standard_text: Cells reproduce by mitosis for growth and repair and by meiosis to make sex cells; organisms reproduce asexually or sexually. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: Living and Non-Living Things)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Living and Non-Living Things): the cell cycle, mitosis, asexual and sexual reproduction, meiosis and stem cells and specialisation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Mitosis copies cells; meiosis makes sex cells.
key_sub: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents.
body_html:
How to think about it

In mitosis one cell divides into two identical cells with the same number of chromosomes. It is used for growth and repair, and for asexual reproduction, where one parent makes offspring that are genetically identical (binary fission, budding, runners, cuttings).

Meiosis makes sex cells (gametes) with half the number of chromosomes: 23 in humans. In sexual reproduction two gametes join at fertilisation, so the offspring get a mix of genes from two parents. This variation helps a population survive change.

Example

A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many does a sperm cell have?

Meiosis halves the number.

Answer: 23

Example

A strawberry plant grows new plants from runners. What kind of reproduction is this?

Only one parent

Answer: asexual

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up mitosis and meiosis.
  • Thinking asexual offspring are different from the parent.
  • Thinking sexual reproduction is faster.

faq.q: What is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
faq.a: It is fast and needs only one parent.
If the environment changes, some individuals may have traits that help them survive.

items.q: Which stage is this? Chromosomes line up in the middle of the cell.
items.e: Metaphase: Chromosomes line up in the middle of the cell.

items.q: What happens in telophase?
c: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
proteins are made for mitosis while the cell keeps growing
nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes
chromosomes line up at the equator (metaphase plate)
items.e: Telophase: nuclear envelopes and nucleoli re-form round each set of chromosomes.

items.q: What happens in cytokinesis?
c: the centromeres split and sister chromatids move to opposite poles
chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form
the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells
DNA replicates and the amount of DNA doubles
items.e: Cytokinesis: the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells.

items.q: In which stage of the cell cycle does this happen: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form?
items.e: Prophase: chromatin condenses into chromosomes and the spindle begins to form.

items.q: Which stage is this? The cell grows and copies its DNA.
items.e: Interphase: The cell grows and copies its DNA.

items.q: Which stage comes right before metaphase?
items.e: Order: interphase, prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase, cytokinesis.

items.q: How does cytokinesis happen in plant cells?
c: a cell plate forms in the middle and grows outward
a furrow forms from the outside
items.e: Animal cells form a cleavage furrow.

items.q: Which cells keep dividing throughout life in plants?
items.e: e.g. root and shoot tips.

items.q: A potato cell has 48 chromosomes. After DNA replication, how many sister chromatids are there?
items.e: Each chromosome is copied: 48 × 2 = 96.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 20 hours. In a sample, 15 of 150 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 15/150 × 1,200 min = 120 min.

items.q: A chimpanzee cell with 48 chromosomes divides by mitosis. How many chromosomes are in both daughter cells together?
items.e: Two cells × 48 = 96.

items.q: How long does a typical human cell cycle take in culture?
items.e: Yeast takes only about 90 minutes.

items.q: A cell cycle lasts 12 hours. In a sample, 45 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Estimate how long mitosis lasts, in minutes.
items.e: Fraction in mitosis × cycle time = 45/400 × 720 min = 81.0 min.

items.q: In a root tip squash, 45 of 400 cells are in mitosis. Calculate the mitotic index as a percentage.
items.e: Mitotic index = cells in mitosis ÷ total cells × 100 = 11.2%.

items.q: Why are offspring from asexual reproduction identical to the parent?
c: They receive a copy of all of one parent's genetic information.
They get half from each of two parents.
items.e: One parent, copied DNA.

items.q: When does a recessive trait appear?
c: when one recessive allele is present
when an organism has two recessive alleles
items.e: For example, bb.

items.q: For meiosis, what is the chromosome number of the daughter cells?
c: identical to each other and the parent
in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: For meiosis, what is where it happens in humans?
c: in the testes and ovaries to make gametes
in body cells for growth and repair
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: For mitosis, what is the number of daughter cells made?
c: in body cells for growth and repair
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: Nonso reads: “A hydra grows a bud that breaks off.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
It will be identical to the parent's.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: For mitosis, what is whether daughter cells are genetically identical?
c: in body cells for growth and repair
identical to each other and the parent
items.e: Mitosis: 2 identical diploid cells for growth and repair. Meiosis: 4 different haploid gametes.

items.q: Compare human sperm and eggs. For a sperm cell, what is the special feature at the front?

a jelly coat that changes after one sperm enters
cannot move by itself; it is moved by cilia in the oviduct
items.e: Sperm: small, many, swim, acrosome. Egg: large, few, food store, moved by cilia.

an acrosome with enzymes to digest the egg's outer layer

items.q: What does a dominant allele do?
c: It needs two copies to show.
It shows its trait even when only one copy is present.
items.e: Shown by a capital letter.

items.q: Zainab reads: “A sea star regrows a whole body from one arm.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: Hadiza reads: “A strawberry plant sends out runners that grow new plants.” How will the offspring's genetic information compare with the parent's?
c: It will be identical to the parent's.
It will be completely random with no parent genes.
It will be a mix of genes from two parents.
items.e: Asexual reproduction copies one parent's DNA; sexual reproduction combines DNA from two parents.

items.q: How many sets of chromosomes does a human get from each parent?
c: one set (23 chromosomes) from each parent

items.q: Kelechi reads: “Two dogs have a litter of puppies.” What type of reproduction is this?
items.e: Asexual: one parent. Sexual: two parents (egg and sperm, or pollen and egg).

items.q: What happens in pachytene of meiosis?
c: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down
chromosomes become visible as thin threads
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
items.e: Pachytene: crossing over takes place at recombination nodules.

items.q: A corn egg and sperm each have 10 chromosomes. How many does the fertilised egg have?
Mitosis: number of divisions?
items.e: Meiosis: two. Mitosis: one.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous pairs line up in the middle of the cell.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A fruit fly cell (2n = 8) finishes meiosis I. How many chromosomes are in each of the two new cells?
items.e: Homologs separate in meiosis I, so each cell has 4 (each still with two chromatids).

items.q: Meiosis: number of divisions?
items.e: Meiosis: two. Mitosis: one.

items.q: What happens in diakinesis of meiosis?
c: sister chromatids separate as the centromere splits
homologous chromosomes pair up (synapsis) to form bivalents
chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down
crossing over takes place at recombination nodules
items.e: Diakinesis: chiasmata terminalise and the nuclear envelope breaks down.

items.q: What is the significance of meiosis?
c: it halves the chromosome number for gametes and creates variation
items.e: Fertilisation restores the diploid number.

items.q: Which stage of meiosis? Homologous chromosomes separate to opposite poles.
items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: Meiosis: main purpose?
items.e: Meiosis: making gametes for sexual reproduction. Mitosis: growth and repair.

items.e: Meiosis I separates homologs; meiosis II separates sister chromatids.

items.q: A horse body cell has 64 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 32.

items.q: A dog body cell has 78 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
A stem cell in bone marrow becomes a red blood cell. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialised.

items.q: What is the genome of an organism?
items.e: The proteome is the set of proteins it can make.

items.q: mRNA: GGCCUUCUU. Codons: CUU = Leu, GGC = Gly, UUU = Phe, CAA = Gln. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: GGC CUU CUU.

items.q: How does decreased acetylation of histones affect a gene?
c: the chromatin becomes more condensed, so transcription is inhibited
items.e: Acetylation loosens chromatin.

items.q: What is the difference between benign and malignant tumours?
c: malignant tumours invade tissues and spread (metastasis)
benign tumours spread around the body
items.e: Benign tumours are usually enclosed.

items.q: What is growing crops with special features, such as disease resistance?
c: a possible future use of stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: mRNA: CGUGGCGGC. Codons: CGU = Arg, GGC = Gly, AUG = Met, GUU = Val. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: CGU GGC GGC.

items.q: mRNA: CAACCUAAA. Codons: AAA = Lys, CAA = Gln, CCU = Pro, GGC = Gly, GUU = Val. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: CAA CCU AAA.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: What is treating diabetes by making insulin-producing cells?
c: a possible future use of stem cells
a use of plant stem cells
a current use of adult stem cells
items.e: Stem cells can divide and differentiate.

items.q: How does increased methylation of DNA affect a gene?
c: it stops transcription factors binding, so the gene is switched off
items.e: Methyl groups are added to cytosine.

items.q: mRNA: UAUCAUCUU. Codons: CAU = His, CUU = Leu, UAU = Tyr, AAA = Lys, UCU = Ser. What is the amino acid sequence?

items.q: mRNA: UGUAUGGCU. Codons: AUG = Met, GCU = Ala, UGU = Cys, UAU = Tyr, CAU = His. What is the amino acid sequence?
items.e: Read the mRNA in triplets from the start: UGU AUG GCU.

items.q: An embryo's cells become heart, nerve and skin cells. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialised.

items.q: Which statement about meristem tissue in plants is true?
c: They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become almost any type of cell.
items.e: It is found at the tips of roots and shoots.

items.q: Which statement about embryonic stem cells is true?
c: They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become almost any type of cell.
items.e: There are ethical objections because embryos are destroyed.

items.q: A skin cut heals as new skin cells are made. Which process is this mainly?
items.e: Mitosis makes more cells; differentiation makes cells specialised.

items.q: Which statement about adult stem cells from bone marrow is true?
c: They can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells.
They can become almost any type of cell.
They can become any type of plant cell throughout the plant's life.
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.

items.q: What does siRNA do?
c: guides an enzyme to cut a complementary mRNA
items.e: The mRNA cannot then be translated.

items.q: Which type of stem cell can become only some types of cell, such as blood cells?
c: adult stem cells from bone marrow
items.e: They are taken from the patient or a donor.
